A retained disposal as durable history, without the two facts that live on the journal rather than in tax-lot storage: the sale&#x27;s effective date and the gain or loss actually booked. RecordedAt is the atomic retention time, not proof that a later replacement window was re-evaluated or finalized.

FaceValueLot owns the par-denominated economics — cost basis, premium/discount, factor-restated face, amortized basis — and this is where those conventions are written onto LedgerTaxLotRecord and read back off it, so a persisted lot can be restated as the aggregate rather than re-derived by each consumer against a hardcoded 100.

A lot&#x27;s own LedgerTaxLotRecord.ParBasis records the basis its price was originally struck in, which is what lets a per-unit quote survive persistence without silently mis-amortizing through math that assumes this one. |

The aggregate and the record must already describe the same acquisition: the record&#x27;s quantity is the face expressed in the engines&#x27; unit convention, so it must equal the aggregate&#x27;s face over LedgerLotParBasis, and cost basis must tie under both readings. |
| <code>public static FaceValueLot? ToFaceValueLot(this LedgerTaxLotRecord record);</code> | [src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/LedgerTaxLotFaceValueTerms.cs:79](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/LedgerTaxLotFaceValueTerms.cs#L79) | Restates a persisted lot as the canonical aggregate, or returns null when the lot recorded no face terms — the lot of record carries them all-three-or-none, and a lot booked before they existed states nothing rather than defaulting to a price-per-100 quote at factor 1. Callers that need face economics must fail closed on the null rather than substituting a quantity. A lot that has absorbed a paydown rehydrates at the factor it currently holds, so its FaceValueLot.FaceOutstanding is the paid-down face; a lot still at its booked factor rehydrates there. |
